subject: Novacorp burst ladder and preemptible fallback cadence for Dedicated
messages:
From: Emma Smith <emma.smith@novacorp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com
Date: 2028-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novacorp: request — burst ladder & fallback cadence for Dedicated

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we flesh out the Dedicated agreement I need a clear operational picture for how Redwood will handle burst traffic above our reserved slab. Specifically:
- How will burst capacity be granted (ephemeral preemptible vs shoulder reserve)?
- What are the autoscale triggers and cooldowns?
- If preemptible nodes are reclaimed, what fallback model variants will you route to and how does that affect latency/SLOs?

We need this captured in an amendment to the SOW so our Procurement and Platform teams can sign off. If you can share a straightforward diagram + policy (thresholds, crediting, eviction behavior) and an expected start date for the amendment that would be ideal.

Also copying ops@novacorp.com who will validate the capacity numbers.

Best,
Emma
Emma Smith
Head of Platform — Novacorp
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Emma Smith <emma.smith@novacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novacorp: request — burst ladder & fallback cadence for Dedicated

Emma — thanks, happy to capture this. I attached a concise proposal (novacorp-burst-ladder-v2.pdf) but the summary below should help the procurement thread.

Proposal (executive summary):
- Ladder approach:
  1) Ephemeral preemptible slab (fastest, lowest-cost) — used first for transient spikes.
  2) Shoulder reserve (short-term reserved capacity) — kicks in for sustained spikes > 10 minutes.
  3) Dedicated reserved pool (your committed slab) — base capacity.
- Autoscale triggers:
  - Preemptible: scale up at sustained queue depth > 60s p50 over 45s window, cool-down 60s, max ramp X GPUs/min (we'll calibrate).
  - Shoulder reserve: step scale when p95 latency breaches 120ms for > 2 min, cool-down 5m.
- Crediting: transient headroom credits (banked against monthly usage) for preemptible bursts; 30% conservative headroom recommended for initial 60 days while we observe traffic patterns.
- Fallback behavior: if preemptible nodes are reclaimed, traffic routes to quantized/half-precision model variant (same family) with a documented latency delta (~10–20% increase) and graceful degradation flags for non-critical routes.
- Observability & ops: telemetry hooks for route-level P50/P95, KV-cache-warm signals, and per-request model variant tags so you can audit regressions.

Next steps: if this aligns I’ll loop in Ben (SLA/finance) and Karthik (capacity) to produce the SOW amendment and capacity model. Proposed start date for the amendment: 2028-05-08 (tentative).

Attachment: novacorp-burst-ladder-v2.pdf (diagram + policy table)

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novacorp: request — burst ladder & fallback cadence for Dedicated

Jasmine — quick technical notes to feed into the SOW and capacity spreadsheet (attached).

1) GPU selection: prefer H100s for the committed slab if Novacorp wants headroom for long-context generation; preemptible layer can be a mix of A100p/RTX-class instances to keep costs predictable.
2) Warm-up & KV cache: sequence-length distribution matters — cold-start penalty can be ~250–400ms for large context models. Recommend a brief prewarm window (30–90s) when shoulder reserve spins up.
3) Autoscale policy specifics:
   - Use step-scaling with conservative upper bounds: add 1–2 GPUs per 60s for preemptible layer, but require sustained metric for 45–60s to avoid flapping.
   - Cooldown: 3m after any scale-up for shoulder reserve to stabilize KV caches.
   - Eviction handling: when preemptible nodes reclaimed, we should drain connections and move active streams to dedicated slab where possible; if not, route to quantized 16-bit variant with lower memory footprint.
4) Headroom %: 30% start, revisit after 60-day telemetry window.

I attached the capacity model (novacorp-capacity-model.xlsx) with two scenarios (steady growth and bursty ecom peak) and recommended tranche sizes. If Procurement wants hard numbers for the SOW we can export scenario 2 (conservative) with explicit GPU counts and fallback latencies.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Dedicated Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emma Smith <emma.smith@novacorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novacorp: request — burst ladder & fallback cadence for Dedicated

Looping in a simplified customer-facing paragraph for the SOW amendment and a couple of business notes:

SOW paragraph (suggested):
  "Redwood will provide a three-tier burst ladder for Novacorp's Dedicated deployment: ephemeral preemptible capacity for transient spikes, shoulder reserve for sustained elevated traffic, and the committed reserved slab for baseline load. Autoscaling thresholds, cooldowns, and fallback model variants are specified in Appendix A. Transient headroom credits will be applied per agreed cadence; Redwood will provide telemetry and weekly usage reports during the initial 60-day observation period."

Business notes:
- SLA credits: falls under standard Dedicated SLA. We can offer a one-time goodwill credit for the first reclaimed preemptible event if Novacorp wants extra assurance.
- Pricing: preemptible bursts billed at blended ephemeral rate; shoulder reserve billable as short-term reservation (invoice line item).

If everyone is aligned I recommend we convert the proposal to a formal amendment and route to Legal / Procurement. Jasmine — can you confirm the final start date and send to Emma for signatures?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Account Executive | Redwood Inference
